thread:
maya: Heads-up — after the scheduler tweak yesterday I'm seeing tail-latency spikes on short-seq traffic. Looks like the kernel chooser is preferring the 'wide-k' path for 1-8 token continuations, which is killing launch overheads. Anyone else?

andre: I saw that in dashboards, +1. 95th p90 jump on the small-chat workload.

kevin: Can you paste the profile? want to see kernel launch vs compute ratio.

maya: pasted below — this is a 50-sample microprofile from the problematic node (p99 requests ~ 20ms extra):

```
# micro-profile summary (sampled stacks)
samples: 50
- kernel_launch: 28 (56%)
- kernel_exec: 12 (24%)
- kv-cache-check: 6 (12%)
- scheduler-overhead: 4 (8%)
avg_seq_len: 6
batch_sizes: median=3, p90=6
dominant_kernel_chosen: wide-k1 (expected skinny-k for short seqs)
```

maya: Notice the huge proportion in kernel_launch. wide-k1 has much larger init overhead but better throughput at length>64 — scheduler is misclassifying due to batching timing.

perf-bot: nightly-profile job finished: nodes/rt-12 shows kernel-launch-regression +12% vs baseline for short sequences. Link: https://perf.redwood/reports/rt-12/1802

andre: Hypothesis: continuous-batching's time-window causes a queued micro-batch to appear larger to the kernel selector (it sees aggregated seq-length distribution) so it picks the high-throughput kernel. But because the real per-request seq lengths are short and KV cache makes many requests fast, effective compute is low -> launch dominates.

sophie: Can we make kernel selector sequence-length-aware at two granularities: per-request and per-microbatch? e.g., if microbatch median seq_len < 16 prefer low-launch kernel, even if computed aggregated flops favors wide-k.

kevin: Agree. Also want to try lightweight online sampling: for first N batches per minute, run both kernels in profiling mode (timing only, dry run) on small batches to estimate launch+exec cost and update a local chooser. No config change needed globally.

maya: Here's a draft autotune config we can try (pseudo):

```
autotune: {
  sample_window_sec: 60,
  sample_rate: 0.05,    # sample 5% of microbatches
  sample_policy: "dual-run-timing", # run kernels w/o committing outputs
  decision_metric: "launch_ms + exec_ms/median_batch",
  hysteresis_ms: 5
}
```

maya: Implementation note — dual-run must be extremely cheap: reuse KV cache lookup and just call kernels with same inputs but skip returning tokens. We must ensure no additional memory blowup.

andre: Alternative quick fix: add a simple rule in scheduler: if median_seq_len <= 16 and median_batch_size <= 8 -> force low-launch kernel. That would be low-risk and immediate.

kevin: I ran a quick sim locally with that rule (on dev machine). p95 dropped back to baseline, p99 improved ~8ms. Tradeoff: small throughput loss for long-seq tails but acceptable for chat workloads.

sophie: Can we combine both: short-term rule + background sampling to remove the rule once autotuner converges?

maya: Yes. Plan: 1) roll rule to canary pool for 2 hours, 2) enable sampling autotune (0.02 rate) on canary nodes, 3) if autotune finds <3ms diff choose persistent rule, else fallback.

kevin: Also add metric emitted: kernel_choice_reason = {auto, rule, manual, sampled} so we can filter dashboards.

perf-bot: created issue #INF-2317: "kernel chooser autotune + short-seq rule" assigned to @kevin, @maya.

andre: Ops note: watch GPU memory transient when dual-run sampling enabled; maybe cap sampled microbatch count if free_mem < 1GB.

maya: I'll prepare the canary patch and a small perf dashboard widget for kern-launch vs exec ratio. If folks agree I'll deploy to canary at 18:15 PT.

sophie: :thumbsup: let's do it. keep the sampling low for safety.

kevin: I'll add the metric tags and implement the hysteresis so we don't flip kernels rapidly.

maya: Thanks — will post the canary link once live.

andre: If canary looks good, we should schedule a broader rollout with rollback gates based on p99 and cost impact.

maya: Agreed. Rolling now to 5% canary (will update thread).

perf-bot: canary-deploy event: 5% nodes, version rt-kchooser-1802 deployed at 1802108200

maya: Canary is live. Early telemetry shows kernel_launch ratio down from 56% -> 22% on canary nodes.

andre: Nice. keep an eye for any long-seq regressions.

kevin: I'll run extended sampling overnight and dump aggregated timings tomorrow morning.

maya: Closing loop tomorrow with results, thanks all.
